title: Amiss external plan
description: The pure derivation `amiss external-plan` makes from one complete scanner report: the distinct destinations delegated to evidence that the candidate introduced and the base lost, each with the documents naming it, bound to the report payload digest the derivation verified. The engine never fetches a destination; the plan only names the work an evidence producer may do.

payload_digest.description: The domain-separated digest of the canonical payload bytes, under the payload schema identity as its domain.

engine.description: The provenance of the binary that derived this plan.

report.description: The one report this plan derives from: its verified payload digest and its own evaluation identities, echoed verbatim so a consumer can join plan, report, and later evidence without re-reading the tree.

base.description: The report's evaluation.base value, echoed verbatim.

candidate.description: The report's evaluation.candidate value, echoed verbatim.

mode.description: The report's evaluation.mode value, echoed verbatim.

introduced.description: Destinations the candidate references and the base does not: the set an evidence producer probes first.

removed.description: Destinations the base referenced and the candidate no longer does.

retained_count.description: Distinct destinations present on both sides, counted and not listed, so the plan stays proportional to the change.

DestinationRow.description: One distinct destination delegated to evidence on the counted side, with every document naming it.

destination.description: The destination after the format's own decoding, exactly as the report records it: what a fetcher would request.

scheme.description: The lowercased request scheme: the occurrence intent's scheme for an external URL, or https for a recognized same-repository forge URL.

documents.description: The repository paths of the documents holding the destination, sorted and unique.

Repository.description: The forge shape of a destination on a known or declared host, structure only: parsed without the other repository's refs, so the revision-and-path tail stays opaque. Absent when the destination is not a recognizable forge repository URL. A verifying layer resolves the tail; this artifact never claims the repository exists.

dialect.description: The URL grammar that split the path: the known-host table's entry, or the report's own declared dialect on its declared host.

owner.description: The owner segments before the name, joined; nested only under the gitlab dialect.

form.description: The path segment after the repository, verbatim: blob, tree, src, issues, whatever the source spelled.

tail.description: Everything after the form, opaque, since branch names may contain slashes and splitting revision from path needs the other repository's refs.
